risks.title: Requirements and scope alignment gaps causing downstream delivery delays
risks.owner: Project Manager / Product Owner / Delivery Lead
risks.reason: Observed repeatedly in filtered data through risks such as 'SOW Scope to fullfilment', 'UAT Readiness by business and Test Scenarios', 'Delay in requirement finalzsation of few features', 'Scope Creep', and 'Story readiness criteria is not evaluated in some cases'.
recommendedActions: Baseline scope-to-requirement traceability before sprint or release start
Require explicit approval for late requirement or scope changes
Track dependency and readiness criteria before committing stories
risks.preventiveActions: Introduce mandatory scope, requirement, and UAT readiness checkpoints before execution windows.
risks.mitigation: Reprioritize scope, defer non-critical items, and maintain traceability from SOW/requirements to user stories and test scenarios.
risks.contingency: Re-baseline timelines and release scope if unresolved requirements or scope changes continue into execution.
relatedHistoricalRisks: UAT Readiness by business and Test Scenarios
Delay in requirement finalzsation of few features
Story readiness criteria is not evaluated in some cases

risks.title: Resource continuity risk in niche or key roles
risks.owner: Engagement Manager / Resource Manager / Delivery Lead
risks.reason: Filtered data contains repeated resource continuity patterns: 'Risk of OT Developer resignation', 'Resigned OT Developer - No Overlap causing risk of timely delivery and revenue loss', 'Critical Resources plan of deployment', and 'Architect Unavailability'.
recommendedActions: Identify backup resources for critical roles
Cross-train ELTs or adjacent team members
Use overlap periods for structured KT before exits or leave
risks.preventiveActions: Maintain succession coverage for niche roles and monitor retention risk proactively.
risks.mitigation: Accelerate backfill, deploy trained backup resources, and document critical operational knowledge.
risks.contingency: Temporarily redistribute work to senior team members and adjust sprint or release commitments.
relatedHistoricalRisks: Resigned OT Developer - No Overlap causing risk of timely delivery and revenue loss

risks.title: Environment, access, and tooling dependencies slowing execution
risks.owner: Technical Lead / Environment Manager / Client IT Coordinator
risks.reason: Evidence exists in filtered data from 'Unable to debug the code as the team works on the VDI.', 'Intermittent Slowness faced with Client VDI', and Volvo environment-planning related items such as 'Dev, QA/Staging and Production Environment mapping...'.
recommendedActions: Track environment and access blockers separately from feature work
Use alternate lower environments or QA recreation paths where possible
Escalate unresolved access/tooling blockers through client governance
risks.preventiveActions: Validate environment readiness and access prerequisites before committing schedules.
risks.mitigation: Use logs, QA samples, alternate environments, and documented workarounds to reduce execution downtime.
risks.contingency: Adjust delivery sequencing to focus on work not blocked by environment or access issues.

strengths: Many filtered historical risks were formally tracked and later closed or resolved.
Several records include specific mitigation plans rather than generic statements.
Volvo and Lenovo closed records provide clear historical evidence for planning and delivery patterns.
weaknesses: Planning and execution governance issues dominate the filtered portfolio.
Resource continuity in niche roles is a repeated pattern, especially in Centene and Lenovo data.
Environment and readiness dependencies continue to affect execution quality and schedule confidence.
lessonsLearned: Scope must be explicitly mapped to requirements before execution begins.
Backlog refinement and definition-of-done clarity reduce downstream UAT and delivery risk.
Critical-role succession and overlap planning are necessary where skills are niche or scarce.
Environment readiness and integration mapping should be completed before test milestones are committed.
successFactors: Early escalation of client-side or external dependencies
Use of backup resources and cross-training for specialized roles
Formal re-baselining when requirement or scope changes are evidenced
Traceable documentation from scope through testing
